about: PLAN's level sequence, Super Mario Bros. on the multicart, one schedule from power-on (docs/plan-log.md). Every field under 'measured' is copied from a log: the planner's (scratch, not committed), the head's run directory on the bench Pi, and tools/check of each run's bridge.log against its own script after the final reset. 'lesson' is authored: what the level made the planner learn.

levels.planner: replay from power-on per candidate (about ten seconds each); about seventy-five minutes, not timed
levels.lesson: A greedy search walks into the first goomba and cannot take it back: backtracking by segment.

levels.planner: saved states (nes branch): a candidate costs its own latches
levels.lesson: Enemy groups need timing (a jump every five latches); a pipe holds Mario longer than the lookahead, and a held segment is no stall.
Keep a move only when a continuation lives (a gentler rule committed Mario to a gap); keep the continuation that found the flagpole.
A castle ends at the axe, not a flagpole: $0770 turns 2, then the next world.
Nothing new.
Swimming (A taps, measured first) and a pipe taken counts above x: past 2-2's exit Mario lands at a smaller x.
Nothing new (the first bench try missed its intro frame: the grabber timed out).
Nothing new: the axe rule held.
The first schedule past the head's room: streamed from latch 19990.
Nothing new.

Beam search: the way on is up, not right, and depth first could not keep that route alive. The first bench try failed on the part, not the plan: the console restarted itself mid-run with a clean poll log (run 20261018-060411).

The model has to stop on the poll, not at the end of the frame: a frame that held two polls let the second fall before the planner gave its byte, so the model played that jump a poll late and the first plan failed its straight replay.

Nothing new. The first bench run played every poll right, but its intro frame was grabbed after the console was switched off (the script ended ten polls after the grab) and it was run again rather than counted (run 20261018-161233).

levels.planner: saved states, --beam 4 --beam-high 1 --no-ceiling, one stretch searched by hand on the model
levels.lesson: Five plans and a hand search: the ceiling leads to a warp zone, the beam needs room for height, a jump has to be able to keep A held across a segment, and a warp is a level change to anywhere but the next level. The last tall pipe was crossed by a route searched by hand on the model and spliced onto the beam's stair-top state.
Nothing new. The beam crossed the mushroom tops and the lifts on its own: once only six positions were alive, and the best of them had gone back, but it went on.

levels.planner: saved states, --beam 4 --beam-high 1, the maze's checks read out of the game; one stretch searched by hand on the model
levels.lesson: A castle maze sends Mario back unless he stands at the height the game's own table wants as the screen reaches a page. The planner now reads that table out of the game's code, calls the loop-back a death, and gives its height slot to the move whose lookahead stands at the wanted height. That crossed the first check on its own; the second is entered only through a one-tile gap that running right crosses, so that stretch was searched by hand and spliced on.
Nothing new: the beam crossed the Bullet Bills and the piranha pipes on its own.
Nothing new: the beam stayed above ground past the Hammer Bros and never took the pipe to the water.
Nothing new: the beam crossed the treetops, the lifts and the Bullet Bills on its own.
Nothing new: the beam crossed World 5's castle, its firebars and Podoboos, on its own.
